rows.n: Beach Road Fish Head Bee Hoon
rows.w: Held the Michelin Bib Gourmand in 2024 and 2025, and widely called one of Singapore's best fish soups: sliced or fried fish-head bee hoon in a rich, milky stock finished with fried garlic. Morning hours only, a few days a week — go early.

Balestier's other chicken-rice institution (alongside Boon Tong Kee): founded in 1953 by Hainanese immigrants and run by three generations, everything made from scratch — silky steamed or crisp-skinned roast chicken over fluffy rice cooked in garlicky chicken broth, with chilli, dark soy and ginger paste. The Loy Kee Special Set is the full Hainanese spread on one tray.

You see the queue before the stall: a Michelin Bib Gourmand (2023) fried Hokkien mee that pairs thick bee hoon with yellow noodles in a slightly wet, umami-laden prawn stock. Open from mid-afternoon into the small hours, it is Whampoa's night-market anchor.
A chicken rice institution since 1979; promoted to Michelin Bib Gourmand in 2025.

rows.n: Amoy St Lor Mee (Best Lu Mian In Town)
rows.w: Whampoa is almost synonymous with this stall and its bold claim to the 'Best Lu Mian In Town': a two-item menu of thick, starchy lor mee laden with ngoh hiang, fish nuggets and braised pork (or the amped-up Jumbo Meal), with long morning queues.

The Taipei beef-noodle shop recognised by the MICHELIN Bib Gourmand in Taipei opened its first overseas outlet here on 13 Feb 2023 — a modern take on Taiwanese braised beef noodles (Seth Lui, Eatbook, Miss Tam Chiak, HungryGoWhere).

Prawn paste chicken is the other order. Reviewers note consistency depends on who is at the wok.

rows.n: Goh Chor Tua Pek Kong Temple & Wayang Stage
rows.w: Balestier's red temple, founded in 1847 by Hokkien labourers on Joseph Balestier's sugar-cane estate ('Goh Chor' = Rochore), rebuilt in southern Chinese style in 1920/1928 — and beside it one of Singapore's last permanent wayang (Chinese opera) stages, built 1906 by Tan Boo Liat and still used by troupes during the Hungry Ghost Festival. Conserved by URA.

rows.n: Former Malay Film Productions Studio (Shaw Studio)
rows.w: Shaw Brothers' Malay Film Productions studio on Jalan Ampas (1947-1969), where more than 150 films — many starring P. Ramlee — were shot in the golden age of Malay cinema. The surviving studio gate and buildings sit at the end of a quiet lane off Balestier Road.

The Loy Kee Special Set is the full Hainanese spread on one tray.

Balestier is Singapore's tau sar piah street, and Loong Fatt (since 1948) is its original — still in the same shophouse with the old tiled walls and floor, wooden tables and booths, baking flaky mung-bean pastries by hand. A stop on the National Heritage Board's Balestier Food Trail.

rows.n: Sun Yat Sen Nanyang Memorial Hall
rows.w: Wan Qing Yuan, the 1880s villa off Balestier Road that Dr Sun Yat Sen used as his Southeast Asian base for the Tongmenghui — now a National Monument whose galleries tell how overseas Chinese communities bankrolled and shaped the 1911 Revolution. Anchor stop on NHB's Balestier Heritage Trail.

rows.n: Maha Sasana Ramsi Burmese Buddhist Temple
rows.w: Singapore's Burmese Buddhist temple, founded on Kinta Road in 1878 and rebuilt beside the Sun Yat Sen villa on Tai Gin Road in 1991 — it houses the largest white-marble Buddha outside Myanmar, carved from a single block of Mandalay marble. On the 'Faith, Film and Food' route of NHB's Balestier Heritage Trail.

The sole surviving rural-market building in Singapore, designed by local architect Kwan Yow Luen with animal-and-flower reliefs across its cream walls — a heritage-trail stop that still trades as a cluster of eateries. A planned April 2025 closure was reversed — the tenancy was extended by two years (Seth Lui, Feb 2025).

The 1973 hawker centre and wet market spread across HDB blocks 90, 91 and 92 on Whampoa Drive — successor to the old Rayman Market and a stop on NHB's Balestier Heritage Trail. Two cooked-food halls side by side hold some of Balestier's best breakfasts: Hoover rojak, fish-head bee hoon, lor mee, Hokkien mee.

rows: 2 places · kept for the record, newest check first

rows.n: Ah Hui Big Prawn Noodle (Balestier Food Centre) — CLOSED
rows.w: Aromatic, umami-rich prawn noodle soup — a slightly sweet, garlicky prawn stock, firm big prawns and optional tender pork ribs ($5) — the headline stall of Balestier's heritage market building in both Seth Lui's and Women's Weekly's Balestier Food Centre guides.

rows.n: Miao Sin Popiah & Carrot Cake — CLOSED
rows.w: CLOSED 26 Feb 2026. Ong Chin Quay's 45-year-old popiah and carrot-cake stall (started 1980 on Upper Boon Keng Road, at Balestier Market since the 2010s) shut when the 72-year-old hawker found no successor (Mothership; Seth Lui). Women's Weekly had named it among Balestier Food Centre's best and Singapore's great popiah stops. Kept here, flagged, as part of the market's record.
